title: A Provision for the Rivergate
premise: Emrys Vasquez, estranged son of archaeologist Dr. Ilsa Vasquez, owes a dangerous debt to the smuggler Corvo and takes a paid job ferrying supplies upriver to her expedition at the Rivergate ruins. When he arrives to find the camp ransacked, the radio dead, and his mother missing, he teams up with Sefa, a river pilot and stranger with her own reasons for hating the expedition's financier. Together they survive the monsoon, uncover that Ilsa faked her disappearance to hide a discovery she believed would be weaponized, and confront Corvo, who has been hunting the site all along. Emrys must choose between paying his debt by handing over the find or destroying it; in the end he burns the evidence, forgives his mother as the flood recedes, and leaves the river with Sefa, free but empty-handed.
about_author: Rafael Okafor is a former river guide who spent six seasons on commercial expeditions before turning to fiction full-time. He writes adventure stories rooted in real waterways, drawing on firsthand knowledge of monsoon travel and the people who make their living on unpredictable rivers.

chapters.title: The Weight of Owed Things
chapters.summary: Emrys Vasquez counts coins in a dockside flophouse while Corvo's enforcer reminds him of the debt left by his father. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: shame sharpened into resolve when a courier delivers a contract — ferry supplies upriver to an expedition led by Dr. Ilsa Vasquez, the mother who abandoned him.

chapters.title: A Boat Named After No One
chapters.summary: Emrys inspects the leaking longboat he's been given and loads crates he isn't allowed to open. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: wary pride as he patches the hull himself, refusing help, establishing the self-reliance that will both save and endanger him.

chapters.title: Upstream Against the Calendar
chapters.summary: The first days of travel; Emrys navigates rapids and notes the dry season deadline printed on his contract. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: uneasy freedom — the river feels like escape until he finds a torn expedition flag snagged on rocks far below the mapped campsite.

chapters.title: The Pilot Who Knows Too Much
chapters.summary: At a trading post, Sefa, a sharp-tongued river pilot, warns him the upper reaches are closed and offers passage through a shortcut — for a price. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: guarded mutual sizing-up; Sefa recognizes the expedition's financier's mark on his crates and says nothing.

chapters.title: Radio Silence
chapters.summary: Emrys tries raising the Rivergate camp on the contract radio each night; static answers. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: dread compounding into obsession as he pushes past the last safe anchorage against every warning.

chapters.title: What the Monsoon Takes First
chapters.summary: The storm hits early. Emrys bails water through the night, losing half his supplies overboard. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: humbling terror — competence means nothing against the river, and survival now depends on luck he doesn't trust.

chapters.title: Strangers in a Leaking Hull
chapters.summary: Sefa finds him adrift near the shortcut mouth and comes aboard; they run the flooded gorge together. POV: alternating Emrys/Sefa. Emotional beat: forced intimacy — two proud people discovering they work well together and resenting how much that matters.

chapters.title: The Ransacked Gate
chapters.summary: They reach the Rivergate camp: tents slashed, equipment stripped, no bodies, and a fresh grave marked with Ilsa's compass. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: grief colliding with disbelief — the compass is his father's, the one Ilsa took when she left.

chapters.title: Sefa's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sefa finally explains herself: the expedition's financier ruined her family's village upstream and she has tracked this dig for years. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: confession as leverage and gift — trust offered with conditions, deepening their alliance.

chapters.title: Tracks That Lie
chapters.summary: Emrys reads the campsite like a dig: the 'grave' holds stones, not bones, and footprints lead inland, deliberately obscured. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: cold hope — his mother may be alive, and may have staged everything, reopening every old wound of abandonment.

chapters.title: Corvo's Wake
chapters.summary: Corvo's gunboat appears downstream; the pair hide the boat and watch armed men search the ruins. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: hunted claustrophobia — Emrys realizes his debt was never about money; Corvo wanted him to lead the way here.

chapters.title: Into the Karst
chapters.summary: Following the trail inland, they cross flooded limestone country and find a hidden cairn of survey markers pointing toward a cave system behind the falls. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: awe braided with anger — Ilsa found something worth killing for and told no one, not even him.

chapters.title: The Dry Season Clock
chapters.summary: Sefa calculates the monsoon will trap them past any rescue window; going forward means months cut off, going back means Corvo. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: quiet commitment — she chooses to stay, and admits it isn't only about revenge anymore.

chapters.title: Chamber of the Second River
chapters.summary: Inside the caves they discover the expedition's true find: a vast subterranean waterway and artifacts proving the Rivergate civilization engineered the flood cycles of the whole valley. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear — he understands why powers upstream would want this buried or owned.

chapters.title: Mother, at Gunpoint of History
chapters.summary: Ilsa emerges from the inner chambers, alive, having faked her death to keep the discovery from her own financier. Mother and son meet after twelve years. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: fury and love detonating together — she chose the work over him once, and is choosing it again.

chapters.title: Three Truths, One Exit
chapters.summary: Ilsa reveals Corvo funded the dig to seize the waterway's engineering records; Sefa learns her village was drowned deliberately to test the old floodgates. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: betrayal stacking on betrayal — loyalty to each other becomes the only clean thing left.

chapters.title: The Bargain Below
chapters.summary: Corvo's men breach the caves; cornered, Emrys offers himself and the records in exchange for letting Sefa and Ilsa go. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: sacrifice as redemption — paying his father's debt with his own freedom, finally owning the choice.

chapters.title: Water Remembers
chapters.summary: Ilsa triggers the ancient sluice mechanism, flooding the lower chambers; in the chaos Emrys seizes the records back and the three flee through rising water. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: desperate exhilaration — using the dead civilization's genius to defeat the living predator.

chapters.title: What Burns
chapters.summary: On a high ledge above the falls, Emrys burns the engineering records rather than sell them or surrender them; Corvo watches from across the gorge, defeated without a shot. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: grief and release — the debt dies in the fire, along with his mother's life's work.

chapters.title: Reckoning at the Gate
chapters.summary: Ilsa faces what she destroyed and what it cost; she and Emrys speak plainly for the first time — no apologies that erase anything, just acknowledgment. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: painful, incomplete reconciliation — forgiveness offered without forgetting.

chapters.title: Downriver
chapters.summary: The monsoon breaks; the three ride the swollen river down to the delta, where Corvo's empire begins collapsing under exposure from Sefa's evidence. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: hard-won peace — justice arrives sideways, imperfect, carried on the current.

chapters.title: A Provision for the Rivergate
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Emrys and Sefa refit the patched boat for honest trade runs; Ilsa stays to document what remains for the historical record, openly this time. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: earned hope — he leaves the river lighter than he came, carrying a compass that points wherever he chooses.
